_about: THE ONE VOCABULARY every Mandate brain describes a company in. This file is the SOURCE: mandate/vocabulary/emit.py generates mandate/vocabulary/generated.py (Python, both brains) and web/lib/mandate/vocabulary.generated.ts (the site), and mandate/vocabulary/check.py fails CI when either is stale or when a brain's own copy (capital types.ts via capital/data/vocabularies.json, capital's classify_taxonomy.TAXONOMY, policy's data/seeds.py SECTORS and questions.py options) disagrees with it. Edit here, run `python3 mandate/vocabulary/emit.py`, commit all three. Values are insert-only: a value a stored profile may hold is never renamed or removed, only added to (a stored profile version names the vocabulary version it was written under).

decisions.decision: Capital's 11 sector families (types.ts SECTOR_OPTIONS, the corpus's NACE-backed sector_top) are the shared sector axis, with capital's Tier-2 subsectors (classify_taxonomy.TAXONOMY) under them, in capital's order and spelling.
decisions.why: An audit judged capital's the stronger definition: it is resolved from the NACE code state-aid registers publish, so a founder's answer joins the award record. Policy's 10 slugs are a hand list with no data behind them.

decisions.decision: Policy's 10 sector slugs are NOT a second axis. Each one is LIFTED to one shared (family, subsector) and DERIVED back from the profile's subsectors, falling back to the family. The table is `policySectors` below; `policySector` on a family or subsector is the derivation.
decisions.why: Both agents must read one description of the company. Policy keeps its slugs (its Sector table and facet queries key on them), but they are computed, never asked.

decisions.decision: fintech -> software_data_ai / fintech (capital's own subsector). blockchain_web3 also derives fintech.
decisions.why: A fintech builds software; that is what capital's corpus files it under. Crypto-asset providers face the financial-services regime (MiCA, DORA) policy's fintech facet retrieves. The aid-law restriction `activities: financial_services` is a DIFFERENT, capital-only fact and is never derived from the sector: a company that sells software to banks is fintech and is not a financial undertaking.

decisions.decision: ecommerce -> software_data_ai / ecommerce_marketplaces, a NEW subsector (origin mandate).
decisions.why: Capital has no commerce subsector; policy needs one (DSA marketplace, product-safety, geo-blocking duties). It sits under software because an online marketplace is what capital's NACE backbone files as information services. origin=mandate keeps it out of capital's classifier enum, so no corpus label moves.

decisions.decision: adtech -> software_data_ai / advertising_adtech, a NEW subsector (origin mandate). Capital's gaming_media also derives adtech.
decisions.why: Policy's slug is 'Advertising & Media'. gaming_media is the closest capital subsector but lifting adtech to it would file every ad vendor as a games studio for capital; a dedicated subsector does not, and media still reaches policy's facet through the derivation.

decisions.decision: healthtech -> health_life_sciences / digital_health; the whole health family derives healthtech.
decisions.why: Policy's facet is medical devices + health data, which bites on medtech, diagnostics and digital health alike; pharma is included because a family-level fallback that skipped part of the family would be a register, not a rule.

decisions.decision: manufacturing -> industrial_manufacturing / industrial_general; semiconductors_electronics also derives manufacturing.
decisions.why: Policy's slug is 'Manufacturing & IoT' and its facet is product safety, CE marking, the CRA and radio equipment, which land on electronics makers as squarely as on machinery makers.

decisions.decision: telecom -> software_data_ai / telecom_networking; space / satellite_comms also derives telecom.
decisions.why: Both are electronic-communications providers in EU law (EECC).

decisions.decision: public-sector -> software_data_ai / govtech.
decisions.why: Policy's facet (accessibility, procurement, open data) is the duty set of a supplier TO the public sector, which is what govtech means. A company that IS a public body is capital's organisationType=public_body, a different fact, not derived from here.

decisions.decision: mobility -> mobility_transport / mobility_general; energy -> energy_cleantech / energy_general; software-saas -> software_data_ai / saas_business_software.
decisions.why: Lift to the family's own *_general escape where policy's slug names a whole family, so the lift claims nothing finer than the founder said.

decisions.decision: space (except satellite_comms), defense_security, agrifood, materials_chemicals and other derive NO policy slug.
decisions.why: Policy has no sector facet for them; a company there still gets every non-sector facet. Adding a policy slug later is one edit here.

decisions.decision: Company size is NEVER asked. It is derived from three bands, headcount, turnover and balance sheet, whose edges are the statutory thresholds: EU SME status per Recommendation 2003/361/EC Art. 2 (staff <10/<50/<250 AND turnover <=2/10/50M OR balance <=2/10/43M), and policy's fifth class `enterprise` at 1,000 staff OR EUR 450M turnover (the CSRD threshold policy's own question already uses).
decisions.why: Policy asked founders to self-declare micro/small/medium/large; capital already asked the three facts the law is made of. A self-declared size is a guess about a legal test; three bands are the test.

decisions.decision: The shared bands REFINE capital's: every capital edge is a shared edge, so each shared band projects onto exactly one capital band (`capital`). Added: headcount 250-999 / 1000+ and turnover 50-450M / >450M (policy's enterprise line), balance 2-10M / 10-43M (the SME small-tier rung capital's ladder lacked). Capital's coarse values (250+, >50M, 2-43M) stay VALID answers, declared as `covers` of the fine ones.
decisions.why: Capital's eligibility outputs are unchanged (the adapter projects), policy's five classes become derivable, and the documented hole in capital's deriveSmeStatus (a 30-staff, EUR 9M-balance company read medium) closes for any profile that answers the finer band.

decisions.decision: A band that straddles a threshold cannot satisfy it (capital's existing rule: 2-43M balance does not prove <=10M). An absent band is 'nothing to go on'. With headcount only, the derivation proves only `large`.
decisions.why: Reproduces capital's deriveSmeStatus exactly on capital's bands (tested exhaustively), and a wrong SME claim in an application is worse than an absent one.

decisions.decision: The linked/partner-enterprise rules (a >25% owner consolidates) are NOT applied.
decisions.why: As in capital's companyProfile.ts: ownerOver25 is asked for exactly that, and wiring it in is its own change.

decisions.decision: Countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in the profile. `name` is capital's spelling (its intake picker and corpus), which the capital adapter emits; `eu` marks member states. Scope is capital's European corpus scope.
decisions.why: Capital matches on full English names, policy on codes; a code with one canonical name serves both, and 'Czech Republic' vs 'Czechia' stops being a join failure.

decisions.decision: `markets` (the jurisdictions whose rules the company faces, EU plus member-state codes) is its own field, read by policy and not by capital. When it is absent it is derived: EU (if established in a member state or nowhere known), plus each policy-supported national jurisdiction the company is established in.
decisions.why: Where a company is established and where it sells are different facts; policy's form asks the second. Deriving only when unasked means a profile written by capital's intake still reaches policy, and a profile written by policy's is untouched.

decisions.decision: developmentStage is capital's four values. Policy does not read it yet.
decisions.why: The stage at which a product is placed on the market is when most product obligations bite; it is in the shared vocabulary so policy can start reading it without a new question.

decisions.decision: Every policy-facing value carries `policyValue`: the exact string policy's web intake sends today (its questions.py option label). The policy adapter emits that string; the lift accepts it and also the short ids profile.py's docstring names (b2b, medium, provider...).
decisions.why: Policy's briefs embed these strings in their retrieval queries, so emitting anything else would change its output. Known defect, NOT fixed here because fixing it changes outputs: profile.py fires the consumer facet on customer_type in {b2c, both}, and the web sends 'consumers (B2C)', so a B2C-only founder never gets it.

decisions.decision: Answers only capital reads (ticket, borrower model, ownership, exclusions, use of funds, region, ...) ride in the profile under `funding`, validated by capital's own vocabulary (types.ts -> capital/data/vocabularies.json), and are not restated here.
decisions.why: One definition each. They move into this file the day a second brain reads one (nonEuControl is the likely first: FDI screening).

size._comment: Bands are [min, max] in staff (inclusive) or EUR millions (max inclusive, min exclusive); null = unbounded. `capital` is the capital band a fine band projects onto; `covers` marks a coarse (capital) band as the union of fine ones. Order is meaning.

enterprise._comment: Splits SME-`large` into policy's large / enterprise. Either test makes an enterprise; a large class needs both known to be below.
